cancer_indication: Adjuvant therapy for node-positive early-stage breast cancer after anthracycline-based regimens and single-agent treatment for metastatic breast cancer after anthracycline failure, used across subtypes including triple-negative breast cancer and HER2-positive disease in combination with trastuzumab.
moa: Paclitaxel binds directly to β-tubulin in microtubules, stabilizing them against depolymerization and blocking the dynamic reorganization required for mitosis, causing G2/M arrest and abnormal multipolar spindles followed by mitotic catastrophe and apoptosis. It also directly binds the anti-apoptotic protein BCL2, inactivating it and facilitating programmed cell death in tumor cells. In breast cancer, paclitaxel perturbs cell-cycle gene programs and induces innate immune and interferon responses while simultaneously activating TLR4-driven NF-κB and PI3K/AKT survival pathways and ABC-transporter–mediated drug efflux that can promote resistance.

HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.description: Gene program controlling the G2/M cell-cycle checkpoint and mitotic entry, including regulators of mitosis and transition through G2 into M phase.
HALLMARK_G2M_CHECKPOINT.interpretation: In breast cancer, this checkpoint underlies proliferative capacity; paclitaxel-induced microtubule stabilization halts mitosis and downregulates G2/M checkpoint genes, contributing to cytotoxicity.

Resistance: High G2/M activity can coexist with robust spindle checkpoints and chromosomal instability programs that let HR+/HER2– and TNBC cells tolerate mitotic errors, reducing paclitaxel lethality.
Swanton et al., Cancer Cell 2007 (mitotic arrest & resistance). PMID: 17560332; Swanton 2009 (CIN and taxane response). PMID: 19458043; Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285 (PubMed)
Sensitive: In many Luminal B and basal-like/TNBC tumors, high G2/M signature reflects many actively dividing cells, increasing the number of mitotic microtubule targets that paclitaxel can kill.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. Nat Rev Cancer. PMID: 15057285 (PubMed); Nakayama et al. (CDK1/2 predicting paclitaxel response). PMID: 19239702

Resistance: Low G2/M transcription means few cells in mitosis at baseline, so paclitaxel’s spindle-targeting MOA has limited opportunity to induce lethal mitotic catastrophe.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285; Samaan et al., Paclitaxel in breast cancer. PMCID: PMC6995578 (PMC)
Sensitive: Some ER–/basal-like tumors with weakened G2/M checkpoints but modest proliferation may still undergo catastrophic mitosis when exposed to paclitaxel despite low baseline G2/M expression.
Wang et al., centrosome/G2M regulators and mitotic catastrophe (cross-cancer; mechanism relevant to taxanes). Tag: cross-cancer mechanistic extrapolation.

Resistance: Persistent or increasing G2/M signature after paclitaxel can indicate adaptive mitotic arrest with survival signaling (e.g., SAC recovery), allowing cells to repair or slip out of mitosis and become resistant.
Swanton et al. 2007. PMID: 17560332; Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285
Sensitive: In sensitive breast tumors, paclitaxel causes pronounced accumulation in mitosis with multipolar spindles and chromosome missegregation; transiently increased G2/M markers reflect lethal mitotic arrest.
Zasadil et al., Sci Transl Med 2014. PMID: 24670687; Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285

Resistance: Loss of G2/M markers after treatment can reflect selection for quiescent or slow-cycling subclones that evade mitotic poisons and drive acquired taxane resistance.
Swanton 2009 (CIN & therapy escape). PMID: 19458043; general taxane resistance reviews in breast cancer.
Sensitive: In highly sensitive tumors, paclitaxel-triggered mitotic catastrophe removes most proliferating cells, so bulk G2/M expression decreases because dividing populations are eliminated.
Zasadil et al. 2014. PMID: 24670687; Samaan et al. 2019 (breast paclitaxel MOA). PMCID: PMC6995578 (PMC)

HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE.description: Genes encoding structural and regulatory components of the mitotic spindle and microtubule apparatus required for chromosome segregation.
HALLMARK_MITOTIC_SPINDLE.interpretation: Breast cancer cells rely on an intact mitotic spindle for division; paclitaxel binding to β-tubulin in spindle microtubules disrupts spindle function and enforces mitotic arrest.

Resistance: Very high spindle gene expression with a “cold” immune phenotype in some TNBCs can associate with intrinsic resistance to neoadjuvant chemo, reflecting proliferative but checkpoint-competent, repair-proficient clones.
Mahner/Reinisch et al., cell-cycle–high TNBC resistance to NAT. BJC/FEBS Open Bio 2021–2023; Weichselbaum IFN/DDIR chemo-resistance signature. PMCID: PMC2587578 (PMC)
Sensitive: In many Luminal B and basal-like tumors, upregulated spindle genes indicate strong dependence on dynamic microtubules, making them ideal targets for paclitaxel-induced spindle defects.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285; Samaan et al. 2019. PMCID: PMC6995578 (PMC)

Resistance: Low spindle gene expression signals few cells traversing mitosis and reduced reliance on mitotic machinery, limiting paclitaxel efficacy.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285
Sensitive: In some genomically unstable basal-like tumors, suppressed spindle signatures can accompany pre-existing spindle defects so that even low-dose paclitaxel tips already fragile mitoses into lethal catastrophe.
Zasadil et al. 2014. PMID: 24670687 (mechanism general but relevant to TNBC taxane response).

Resistance: A rise in spindle genes after paclitaxel may reflect enrichment of subclones that maintain spindle integrity via altered tubulin isotypes or checkpoint rewiring, escaping lethal arrest.
Zhang 2014 paclitaxel review. PMID: 24790459 (Taylor & Francis Online); microtubule drug resistance reviews (cross-cancer extrapolation).
Sensitive: In sensitive breast tumors, paclitaxel causes mitotic accumulation with abnormal spindle morphology, so mitotic spindle transcripts remain high as cells proceed to apoptosis.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285; Zasadil et al. 2014. PMID: 24670687

Resistance: Strong downregulation of spindle genes post-therapy can mark selection for non-cycling, EMT-like, or stem-like cells that no longer rely on mitotic spindles, contributing to relapse in TNBC.
Błaszczak et al., TNBC progression & drug resistance. Cancers 2025. (MDPI)
Sensitive: Collapse of spindle gene expression after treatment may indicate that paclitaxel has effectively cleared mitotically active populations, leaving mainly non-proliferative residual cells.
Samaan et al. 2019. PMCID: PMC6995578; Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285

HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.description: Core regulators and effectors of programmed cell death, including pro- and anti-apoptotic factors.
HALLMARK_APOPTOSIS.interpretation: Activation of apoptosis in breast tumor cells, facilitated by paclitaxel-mediated BCL2 inactivation and mitotic catastrophe, is a key mediator of treatment response.

Resistance: High apoptosis signatures can reflect counterbalancing overexpression of anti-apoptotic proteins (e.g., BCL-2 in Luminal A/B), which buffer paclitaxel-induced damage and confer taxane resistance.
Ruvolo 2001 (BCL-2 phosphorylation & survival). PMID: 11238947 (Nature); Pan et al., paclitaxel–BCL-2 interactions in breast cancer. PMID: 24596623 (MDPI)
Sensitive: TNBC and HER2+ tumors with high baseline pro-apoptotic priming (e.g., BAX/BAK, low BCL-2) more readily convert paclitaxel-induced mitotic stress into caspase-dependent apoptosis.
Miller et al., BAK-dependent paclitaxel apoptosis. PLoS One 2013. PMID: 23593244 (PLOS); Noh et al., intrinsic apoptosis in paclitaxel-treated breast cancer. PMCID: PMC4914213 (PMC)

Resistance: Low apoptotic gene expression (e.g., high BCL-2/MCL-1, low BAX/BAK) characterizes many HR+/HER2– tumors and is a classic mechanism of taxane chemoresistance.
Kaboli et al., chemoresistance & survival pathways in breast cancer. PMCID: PMC8569340 (PMC); Pan et al. 2014. PMID: 24596623 (MDPI)
Sensitive: In some gBRCA/HRD+ tumors, reduced basal apoptotic noise together with high DNA damage and mitotic stress after paclitaxel may favor an abrupt, switch-like apoptotic response when thresholds are exceeded.
Conceptual integration based on BRCA/HRD taxane responsiveness (cross-cancer DNA damage biology); Weichselbaum IFN/DNA damage signature. PMCID: PMC2587578 (PMC)

Resistance: Transient apoptosis pathway activation that quickly attenuates, with surviving cells upregulating BCL-2/MCL-1, can select for resistant clones despite an early spike in apoptotic markers.
Song et al., phosphorylation-regulated BCL-2 network. Br J Pharmacol 2019. PMID: 31001901 (bpspubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com)
Sensitive: In sensitive breast tumors, paclitaxel directly perturbs BCL-2 family proteins, triggers mitochondrial outer membrane permeabilization, and robustly upregulates caspase/apoptosis genes leading to cell death.
Srivastava et al., BCL-2 loop deletion blocks paclitaxel apoptosis. PNAS 1999. PMID: 10097135 (PNAS); Miller 2013. PMID: 23593244 (PLOS)

Resistance: Downregulation of apoptosis genes after exposure indicates that surviving HR+/HER2– or TNBC cells have adapted by upregulating survival pathways (PI3K/AKT, NF-κB), promoting paclitaxel resistance.
Kaboli 2021. PMCID: PMC8569340 (PMC); Dong 2021. Front Pharmacol. PMCID: PMC7886139 (Frontiers)
Sensitive: In some gBRCA/HRD+ contexts, massive early apoptosis removes most tumor cells; later time-point bulk RNA shows reduced apoptotic transcription simply because few viable cancer cells remain.
Clinical taxane benefit in BRCA1/2-mutated breast cancer (cross-trial observation); Pan 2014, paclitaxel apoptosis dynamics. PMID: 24596623 (MDPI)

HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.description: Interferon-γ–responsive genes involved in innate and adaptive immune activation, antigen presentation, and antiviral defense.
HALLMARK_INTERFERON_GAMMA_RESPONSE.interpretation: Paclitaxel can induce interferon-stimulated gene programs in triple-negative breast cancer, and tumors with stronger interferon responses show improved sensitivity to the drug.

Resistance: Chronic IFN-γ signaling can induce PD-L1 and immunosuppressive myeloid programs, leading to immune editing and reduced benefit from chemotherapy alone in some ER– tumors (mechanism cross-cancer but relevant to TNBC).
Weichselbaum et al., IFN-related DNA damage resistance signature. PMCID: PMC2587578 (PMC); Brockwell 2019, IFN/STAT1 and chemo response. (Nature)
Sensitive: In many TNBC and HER2+ cases, IFN-γ–high, T-cell–inflamed tumors have better prognosis and respond more to taxane-containing chemo, reflecting active antitumor immunity.
Cheng et al., GBP5 as taxane-benefit marker in TNBC. J Pers Med 2021. PMCID: PMC8003939 (MDPI); Legrier/Weichselbaum ER- breast chemo response. PMCID: PMC2587578 (PMC)

Resistance: IFN-γ–low, immune-cold HR+/HER2– or TNBC tumors lack effective T-cell help and show poorer response to neoadjuvant paclitaxel-based regimens.
Immune activity predicting paclitaxel response in GeparSepto (G7) trial. NCT01583426 (ResearchGate); Heimes et al., high IFN-γ and survival in breast cancer. (Frontiers)
Sensitive: Some chemo-naïve luminal tumors with low IFN-γ but intact ER-driven biology may still be chemosensitive because proliferation rather than immunity dictates paclitaxel response.
Reinisch et al., node-positive early BC receiving taxanes. FEBS Open Bio 2023. (FEBS Journal)

Resistance: Sustained post-treatment IFN-γ can drive PD-L1 and other checkpoints, establishing adaptive immune resistance that limits long-term benefit of chemotherapy alone.
Jin 2024, PD-1/PD-L1 blockade in breast cancer. Mol Cancer 2024. (BioMed Central); IFN-γ–driven PD-L1 expression in ICI literature (cross-cancer). (JCI)
Sensitive: Metronomic paclitaxel in TNBC enhances IFN-γ–driven T-cell activity and improves PD-1 mAb efficacy, indicating that drug-induced IFN-γ signaling can mark chemosensitivity and immunotherapy synergy.
Chen et al., metronomic paclitaxel + PD-1 in TNBC. Am J Transl Res 2020. PMCID: PMC7061845 (PMC)

Resistance: Failure to induce or maintain IFN-γ signatures after paclitaxel suggests a persistently immune-excluded microenvironment, which is associated with poor response to chemo-immunotherapy in TNBC.
Syeda 2025, immune monitoring of chemo-immunotherapy in breast cancer. (Frontiers); Blaye 2022, immune signature and TNBC relapse. (esmoopen.com)
Sensitive: In responders, effective clearance of tumor cells and normalization of inflammation can lower IFN-γ pathway expression over time, despite an initially favorable immune activation.
Conceptual post-response normalization; supported by longitudinal immune-gene monitoring in early TNBC (chemo-ICI trials). (AACR Journals)

REACTOME_NFKB_AND_MAP_KINASES_ACTIVATION.description: Toll-like receptor 4 signaling cascade that activates NF-κB and MAP kinase pathways, leading to transcription of inflammatory cytokines such as IL6 and IL8.
REACTOME_NFKB_AND_MAP_KINASES_ACTIVATION.interpretation: In breast cancer cells, paclitaxel agonism of TLR4 activates NF-κB/MAPK survival signaling and cytokine production, driving inflammatory, pro-survival states associated with chemoresistance.

Resistance: TNBC and other subtypes with high TLR4/NF-κB/MAPK signaling express IL-6/IL-8 and anti-apoptotic genes, showing poor response to paclitaxel.

Rajput et al., “TLR4 is a novel determinant of the response to paclitaxel in breast cancer.” Mol Cancer Ther 2013. PMID: 23720768 (PubMed); Li 2025, TLR4-mediated chemoresistance review. (SpringerLink)
Sensitive: In rare contexts, moderate TLR4/MAPK activation in immune cells can promote antigen presentation and T-cell priming so that taxane-induced tumor death is amplified by NF-κB–driven immune activation (cross-cancer immunology extrapolation).
Immune-based mechanisms of chemotherapy. Cell Death Differ 2013. PMID: 23852325 (Nature)

Resistance: Very low TLR4/NF-κB activity can also be unfavorable when it reflects anergic tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells and poor innate immune sensing of dying cells, limiting immunogenic paclitaxel responses.
Immune-chemotherapy interaction reviews (cross-cancer). Cell Death Differ 2013. PMID: 23852325 (Nature)
Sensitive: In TLR4-low breast tumors, paclitaxel acts mainly as a pure mitotic poison without triggering strong NF-κB pro-survival signaling, leading to better chemo response.
Rajput et al. 2013. PMID: 23720768 (PubMed); Ge et al., PFKFB3–TLR4 axis and paclitaxel resistance in breast cancer. Cell Mol Biol 2016. (cellmolbiol.org)

Resistance: Paclitaxel ligates TLR4 on breast cancer cells, activating NF-κB/MAPK and inducing cytokines that promote survival, invasion, and resistance, especially in TNBC.
Rajput et al. 2013. PMID: 23720768 (PubMed); Li 2025 TLR4 chemoresistance review. (SpringerLink)
Sensitive: When NF-κB/MAPK activation occurs predominantly in antigen-presenting cells rather than tumor cells, paclitaxel-induced TLR4 stimulation can enhance antitumor immunity and potentiate response (tag: mechanism shown mainly in murine models).
Muraro 2023 & Bravetti 2023, metronomic chemo and immune activation. (MDPI)

Resistance: Strong pharmacologic or adaptive suppression of NF-κB/MAPK in immune cells may blunt dendritic maturation and T-cell priming, limiting long-term benefit from taxane-based chemo-immunotherapy.
Immunomodulation with metronomic chemo (cross-cancer). Front Immunol 2015. PMID: 26500631 (Frontiers)
Sensitive: In TLR4-positive tumors, inhibiting or down-modulating NF-κB/MAPK after paclitaxel (e.g., via PFKFB3/TLR4 targeting) restores apoptosis and improves paclitaxel sensitivity.
Sootichote et al., TLR4 inhibition sensitizes to paclitaxel. BMC Cancer 2018. PMID: 29661103 (BioMed Central); Ge et al. 2016 (PFKFB3–TLR4). (cellmolbiol.org)

REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING.description: Phosphoinositide 3-kinase and AKT kinase signaling network that promotes cell survival, metabolism, and growth.
REACTOME_PI3K_AKT_SIGNALING.interpretation: Paclitaxel-induced TLR4 or growth factor receptor activation can stimulate PI3K/AKT survival signaling in breast tumors, helping cells evade paclitaxel-triggered apoptosis.

Resistance: Constitutive PI3K/AKT activation (PIK3CA mutation, PTEN loss) in HR+/HER2– and TNBC upregulates survival and anti-apoptotic effectors, conferring broad chemoresistance including to paclitaxel.
Kaboli et al., PI3K/AKT and chemoresistance in breast cancer. PMCID: PMC8569340 (PMC); Miricescu et al., PI3K/AKT in breast cancer. Int J Mol Sci 2020. (MDPI)
Sensitive: In some highly proliferative HER2+ or Luminal B cancers, strong PI3K/AKT signaling coexists with rapid cell-cycle progression, increasing mitotic entry and thus paclitaxel-targetable cells despite partial survival signaling.
Yuan et al., PI3K–AKT-targeting in breast cancer. PMCID: PMC9856042 (PMC) (conceptual extrapolation)

Resistance: Very low PI3K/AKT signaling may reflect dormant or senescent cell populations rather than apoptotic priming, reducing dependence on mitotic proliferation and limiting paclitaxel efficacy.
Dong 2021, PI3K/AKT and drug resistance (cross-cancer). PMCID: PMC7886139 (Frontiers)
Sensitive: Tumors with low PI3K/AKT activity often have reduced anti-apoptotic buffering, so paclitaxel-induced damage more readily triggers BAX/BAK-dependent apoptosis.
Kaboli 2021. PMCID: PMC8569340 (PMC); Hu et al., PI3K inhibitor overcoming MDR in breast cancer. Cell Death Dis 2015. PMID: 26492368 (Nature)

Resistance: Paclitaxel stress can activate RTKs and cytokine receptors leading to rebound PI3K/AKT signaling, which supports survival, cancer stem-cell maintenance, and acquired resistance.
Kaboli 2021. PMCID: PMC8569340 (PMC); Dong 2021. PMCID: PMC7886139 (Frontiers)
Sensitive: Transient AKT activation during mitotic arrest may co-occur with overwhelming pro-apoptotic signaling (MCL-1 loss, BAK activation), so that despite AKT up-tics, cells still commit to death in paclitaxel-sensitive tumors.
Miller 2013, BAK-dependent paclitaxel apoptosis. PMCID: PMC3616069 (PLOS)

Resistance: Profound AKT pathway suppression after treatment can select for clones that rely on alternative survival routes (e.g., NF-κB, autophagy), resulting in complex multidrug resistance.
Dong 2021. PMCID: PMC7886139 (Frontiers)
Sensitive: In many responding HR+/HER2– tumors, effective paclitaxel treatment is associated with decreased PI3K/AKT signaling and restored apoptosis, consistent with pathway downregulation marking sensitivity.
Hu 2015, BKM120 overcoming MDR via PI3K/AKT/NF-κB inhibition. PMID: 26492368 (Nature); Kaboli 2021 (PMC)

KEGG_CYTOKINE_CYTOKINE_RECEPTOR_INTERACT.description: Cytokines and their receptors, including IL6 and IL8, mediating intercellular communication and inflammatory responses.
KEGG_CYTOKINE_CYTOKINE_RECEPTOR_INTERACT.interpretation: Paclitaxel/TLR4-driven upregulation of IL6, IL8, and other cytokines in breast cancer cells creates autocrine survival and pro-angiogenic loops that support resistance and tumor progression.

Resistance: A cytokine profile dominated by IL-6/IL-8/TNF-α in TNBC fosters EMT, stemness, and drug resistance, reducing paclitaxel benefit.
KEGG hsa04060 (cytokine–cytokine receptor interaction). (KEGG); Błaszczak 2025 TNBC review (IL-6/IL-8 and resistance). (MDPI)
Sensitive: Conversely, Th1/IFN-γ/IL-12-rich cytokine signatures associated with T-cell–inflamed TNBC correlate with better response to taxane-containing chemotherapy.
Opdam et al., immune gene sets and taxane benefit. Clin Cancer Res 2024. (PMC); KEGG hsa04060 (KEGG)

Resistance: Low cytokine–receptor activity indicates an immune-cold microenvironment with poor recruitment of effector cells, often linked to suboptimal response to paclitaxel-based chemo.
GeparSepto immune-activity analysis (paclitaxel response). NCT01583426 (ResearchGate)
Sensitive: Some highly proliferative Luminal B tumors with limited immune infiltration still respond to taxanes, where cell-intrinsic mitotic rate outweighs cytokine context.
Reinisch 2023, dose-dense vs standard adjuvant chemo. (FEBS Journal)

Resistance: Paclitaxel-induced cytokines like IL-6/IL-8 can recruit immunosuppressive myeloid cells and promote angiogenesis, driving late resistance and metastasis.
Volk-Draper et al., paclitaxel promoting breast cancer metastasis via TLR4/IL-8. PMCID: PMC4185415 (Europe PMC); KEGG hsa04060 (KEGG)
Sensitive: Metronomic paclitaxel modulates cytokines to enhance antitumor immunity and improve PD-1 blockade efficacy in TNBC.
Chen et al. 2020, metronomic PTX + PD-1 in TNBC. PMCID: PMC7061845 (PMC); Liu 2025, metronomic chemo in breast cancer. (PubMed)

Resistance: Failure of cytokine–receptor pathway activation post-therapy suggests absence of immunogenic cell death and may mark tumors that remain uninflamed and resistant to further therapy.
Muraro 2023, metronomic chemotherapy anti-tumor pathways. Cancers 2023. (MDPI)
Sensitive: In responding tumors, reduction of inflammatory cytokines after initial activation can reflect resolution of effective antitumor responses and tumor burden decline.
Bravetti 2023, metronomic chemo & immune modulation. (ScienceDirect)

KEGG_ABC_TRANSPORTERS.description: ATP-binding cassette transporter family members that mediate active transmembrane efflux of xenobiotics and drugs.
KEGG_ABC_TRANSPORTERS.interpretation: Overexpression of ABC transporters such as ABCB1 and ABCC3 in breast cancer enhances paclitaxel efflux, lowering intracellular drug levels and conferring chemoresistance.

Resistance: Overexpression of ABCB1/P-gp, ABCC1, and ABCG2 in TNBC actively effluxes paclitaxel and underlies multidrug resistance.
Abd El-Aziz et al., ABCB1 and chemoresistance in TNBC. PMCID: PMC7909869 (PMC); Immunotherapy resistance in TNBC (ABC overexpression). (Frontiers); KEGG hsa02010 (PubMed)
Sensitive: If high ABC transporter expression is restricted to stromal or immune compartments rather than tumor cells (rare, context-dependent), tumors may still be taxane-sensitive while host cells handle drug detoxification (speculative, cross-cancer).
van der Pol 2003, ABC transporters in chemo outcome. PMID: 12604403 (PubMed)

Resistance: ABC-low tumors can still be paclitaxel-resistant if alternative mechanisms (PI3K/AKT, TLR4/NF-κB, EMT) dominate; low transporter levels alone do not guarantee sensitivity.
Dong 2021, PI3K/AKT and MDR. PMCID: PMC7886139 (Frontiers); Li 2025 TLR4 chemoresistance review. (SpringerLink)
Sensitive: Low ABC transporter expression in HR+/HER2– and TNBC generally predicts higher intracellular paclitaxel accumulation and better tumor kill.
Abd El-Aziz 2021. PMCID: PMC7909869 (PMC); Xie 2021, metronomic chemo efficacy (M-CT and overcoming resistance). (Lippincott Journals)

Resistance: Paclitaxel exposure can induce ABCB1/ABCG2 expression and select for high-efflux cells, decreasing intracellular drug and driving acquired resistance.
Abd El-Aziz 2021. PMCID: PMC7909869 (PMC); Famta 2021, overcoming P-gp. (ScienceDirect)
Sensitive: Early treatment cycles may transiently upregulate ABC transporters in dying cells; however, if induction is insufficient to prevent apoptosis, this uptrend still occurs in globally sensitive tumors.
Conceptual adaptive response; consistent with ABC induction under cytotoxic stress (AML and solid tumor MDR). van der Pol 2003. PMID: 12604403 (PubMed)

Resistance: Selection for ABC-independent resistance mechanisms (e.g., tubulin isotype change, enhanced repair) can yield paclitaxel-resistant clones with relatively low ABC expression.
Taxane resistance reviews (cross-cancer). Zhang 2014. PMID: 24790459 (Taylor & Francis Online)
Sensitive: Pharmacologic or epigenetic suppression of ABCB1/ABCG2 during therapy increases paclitaxel retention and restores sensitivity in MDR breast cancer models.
Famta 2021, P-gp inhibitor co-delivery. (ScienceDirect); Hu 2015, PI3K inhibition partly reversing MDR. PMID: 26492368 (Nature)

REACTOME_CELL_CYCLE.description: Integrated network of genes regulating progression through all phases of the cell cycle, including checkpoints and mitotic control.
REACTOME_CELL_CYCLE.interpretation: Paclitaxel treatment in triple-negative breast cancer suppresses broad cell-cycle gene expression, aligning with G2/M arrest and reduced proliferation in breast cancer cells.

Resistance: In some TNBC cohorts, extremely high cell-cycle signatures combined with immune-cold phenotype predict resistance to standard neoadjuvant chemo including taxanes.
Nature Commun 2021 TNBC recurrence biomarkers. (Nature); De Marchi 2021 proteogenomic cell-cycle phenotypes. (ACS Publications)
Sensitive: More commonly, high proliferation (Luminal B, basal-like) increases the fraction of cells entering mitosis, which enhances paclitaxel efficacy.
Jordan & Wilson 2004. PMID: 15057285 (PubMed); Reinisch 2023, adjuvant anthracycline/taxane benefit. (FEBS Journal)

Resistance: Low cell-cycle activity typifies indolent Luminal A disease with relatively poor incremental benefit from high-dose taxane therapy.
Miricescu 2020, AKT pathway and proliferation in breast cancer. (MDPI)
Sensitive: Some slowly proliferating but genomically unstable tumors may still be vulnerable, because paclitaxel-induced mitotic errors are catastrophic for the small fraction that do divide.
Zasadil 2014 (multipolar spindle–mediated kill). PMID: 24670687

Resistance: Tumors escaping paclitaxel may re-enter the cell cycle with elevated proliferation signatures, representing aggressive, drug-tolerant clones that drive relapse.
Błaszczak 2025 TNBC progression review. (MDPI)
Sensitive: In early time-points, accumulation of cells at mitosis and S/G2 following paclitaxel reflects effective checkpoint activation preceding apoptosis.
Samaan 2019, paclitaxel’s cell-cycle effects in breast cancer. PMCID: PMC6995578 (PMC)

Resistance: Deep suppression of cell-cycle genes after incomplete tumor kill can mark shift toward quiescent or senescent but viable populations that are relatively taxane-insensitive.
Dong 2021, dormancy and resistance (PI3K/AKT/mTOR). PMCID: PMC7886139 (Frontiers)
Sensitive: In good responders, loss of cycling tumor cells after paclitaxel leads to marked downregulation of cell-cycle programs in residual tissue.
Samaan 2019. PMCID: PMC6995578 (PMC)

HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.description: Gene set controlling new blood vessel formation, including pro-angiogenic growth factors and cytokines.
HALLMARK_ANGIOGENESIS.interpretation: Paclitaxel-induced TLR4/NF-κB activation increases IL6 and IL8, which can promote angiogenesis and breast tumor progression, aligning this pathway with drug resistance.

Resistance: Strong VEGF/angiogenesis signatures often accompany aggressive, chemoresistant disease and can sustain tumor growth despite paclitaxel.
Bocci et al., anti-angiogenic basis of metronomic chemo. Nat Rev Cancer 2003. (Nature); Tao et al. 2015, VEGF/TSP-1 in metronomic PTX. PMID: 25552929 (PubMed)
Sensitive: In some HR+/HER2– and HER2+ tumors, a well-perfused angiogenic vasculature may initially improve paclitaxel delivery, enabling good short-term responses despite pro-angiogenic signaling.
PNAS 2015, vascular normalization and chemo benefit. PMID: 25870253 (PNAS)

Resistance: Poorly angiogenic, hypoxic regions with abnormal vasculature may be underperfused, limiting paclitaxel access and causing primary resistance.
Angiocrine/pericrine signaling and therapy resistance. Physiol Rev 2024. (Physiological Reviews)
Sensitive: Moderately low angiogenesis in small, early-stage tumors can indicate less aggressive biology, where standard-dose paclitaxel is sufficient to control disease.
Fares 2020, metronomic chemo in advanced breast cancer. (ScienceDirect)

Resistance: Paclitaxel can paradoxically promote pro-angiogenic cytokines via TLR4/NF-κB in some models, enhancing metastatic potential and resistance.
Volk-Draper et al., paclitaxel therapy promotes breast cancer metastasis. PMCID: PMC4185415 (Europe PMC)
Sensitive: Transient vascular normalization with functional angiogenesis during therapy can improve drug delivery and oxygenation, augmenting paclitaxel efficacy when not accompanied by strong pro-survival signals.
Bocci 2003 anti-angiogenic basis of metronomic chemo. (Nature); PNAS 2015 vascular normalization. (PNAS)

Resistance: Strong anti-angiogenic pressure can select for highly hypoxic, glycolytic, and invasive clones that withstand paclitaxel and contribute to late relapse.
Muraro 2023, metronomic chemo anti-tumor pathways. Cancers 2023. (MDPI)
Sensitive: Low-dose metronomic paclitaxel reduces VEGF and increases TSP-1, directly targeting tumor endothelium and suppressing angiogenesis, which correlates with durable responses in HR+/HER2– and TNBC.
Tao et al. 2015. PMID: 25552929 (PubMed); Liu 2025, metronomic chemotherapy in breast cancer. (PubMed)

sensitivity_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Tumors with intact p53 have stronger apoptotic signaling, and the report notes that intact p53 favors paclitaxel sensitivity when mitotic arrest triggers cell death.

sensitivity_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Low BCL2 expression reduces anti-apoptotic buffering, and the report states that low BCL2 favors sensitivity to paclitaxel-induced apoptosis.
TLR4 knockdown in triple-negative breast cancer downregulated NF-κB/IL6 survival genes and reduced the paclitaxel IC50, indicating that reduced TLR4 signaling increases sensitivity.
Downregulation or loss of ABCB1/P-glycoprotein increases intracellular paclitaxel retention; clinical data link high ABCB1 expression to resistance, implying that its loss confers sensitivity.
Reduced ABCC3 (MRP3) expression decreases efflux of paclitaxel, and the report notes that loss of ABC transporters like ABCC3 confers sensitivity.

resistance_genes_up_annotations.interpretation: Overexpression of TLR4 and activation by paclitaxel leads to NF-κB/MAPK signaling and secretion of IL6 and IL8, generating pro-survival inflammatory states and chemoresistance.
Elevated ABCB1/P-glycoprotein actively exports paclitaxel from breast cancer cells, lowering intracellular drug levels and driving resistance.
Increased ABCC3 (MRP3) expression enhances paclitaxel efflux, contributing to decreased efficacy and resistance.
Paclitaxel/TLR4 signaling upregulates IL6, which participates in autocrine survival and angiogenic feedback loops linked to resistance and metastasis.
Paclitaxel-induced IL8 secretion as part of the TLR4/NF-κB response promotes pro-survival and pro-angiogenic signaling associated with chemoresistance.
Upregulation of anti-apoptotic BCL2 in highly proliferative tumors is described as contributing to chemoresistance by blunting paclitaxel-induced cell death.

resistance_genes_down_annotations.interpretation: Loss or downregulation of p53 is reported to blunt paclitaxel’s effect, with tumors lacking functional p53 being more chemoresistant.
Downregulation of pro-apoptotic BAX as part of reduced apoptotic machinery is noted as a mechanism that diminishes paclitaxel efficacy and contributes to resistance.

notes: Most mechanistic sensitivity and resistance data summarized here derive from breast cancer models, particularly triple-negative breast cancer, and may not fully generalize to all subtypes. Paclitaxel is contraindicated in patients with a history of severe hypersensitivity to paclitaxel or to Cremophor EL/polyoxyethylated castor oil and requires caution with hepatic dysfunction; see cited regulatory labels and mechanistic reviews for full context.
